findings.text: Removing 'assert new_inode != first_inode' fixes the flake the prior review named, but leaves the case vacuous on exactly the filesystems that motivated the removal: where the kernel hands the freed inode back, first_inode == new_inode, so recorded_service_lock_inode(...) == new_inode holds even under the previous-inode preference this case exists to catch. inode-negative-control.log shows the assertion fires only because that run's filesystem allocated 207179 for the remade file against the recorded 207169. Skip rather than pass when the inode was reused — `if new_inode == first_inode: pytest.skip(...)` — so a silent pass cannot be read as the guard having run.
